rules: Return strict JSON only. No markdown.
You may improve executive language, sequencing, and business framing.
Keep each rewritten field concise. Prefer one or two direct sentences.
Do not invent facts, dollar values, funding status, readiness, realized value, ROI, savings, finance attestation, or production readiness.
Do not expose raw source IDs, file names, adapter IDs, or internal schema labels in user-facing prose.
Do not use V6, V7, dossier, projection, substrate, bridge, or runtime jargon.

Promised value is not realized value. AI spend is non-additive unless explicitly stated otherwise.

budget_posture.source_rule: SUM atomic fy26_budget_line rows in 08_it_budget_spend_value.csv only.

ai_spend_lens.caveat: AI-tagged spend is a lens over existing budget rows and does not increase the $650M total.

story_blocks_to_rewrite.title: The Tower budget posture is source-backed at $650M from atomic budget rows.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.executive_summary: Tower should show $650.0M FY26 technology budget from atomic budget rows only. Run is $487.5M and change is $162.5M.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.business_meaning: The dashboard can discuss budget posture because it traces to atomic budget facts; it cannot reuse retired planning values.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.what_context_reveals: The budget model separates additive atomic budget facts from context, narrative, allocation-only, candidate, and benefit-value rows.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.why_it_matters: This prevents double counting and keeps CIO/CFO budget views reconciled.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.evidence_boundary: Budget is source-backed synthetic demo data; it is not a production financial filing.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.recommended_next_action: Keep Tower totals pinned to atomic budget facts and route benefit claims through the benefits-validation gate.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.measurement_posture: Budget posture is measurable; value realization remains gated.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.value_claim_boundary: Do not render realized value unless finance validation permits it.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.cio_implication: Use the split to decide which run costs can be optimized without starving change programs.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.cfo_implication: Finance can audit each Tower budget amount back to the curated budget view and finance extract rows.

story_blocks_to_rewrite.title: Run consumes three quarters of the FY26 budget, so change capacity must be protected deliberately.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.executive_summary: The source-backed split is $487.5M run and $162.5M change. That is 75% run and 25% change inside the $650.0M FY26 budget.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.business_meaning: Tower should help the CIO see whether mandatory run commitments crowd out transformation capacity.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.what_context_reveals: Run and change are carried as separate numeric source columns on atomic budget rows, so no missing run/change flag is required.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.why_it_matters: A CFO can audit the split without trusting a narrative rollup.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.evidence_boundary: This is budget posture only, not a realized outcome.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.recommended_next_action: Inspect run-heavy categories and ask which commitments can be renegotiated, automated, or retired.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.measurement_posture: Budget split is source-backed; optimization value is not yet proven.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.value_claim_boundary: No savings claim from run reduction until actuals and baselines exist.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.cio_implication: Protect change capacity before adding new AI commitments.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.cfo_implication: Use the run/change split as the opening budget-control conversation.

story_blocks_to_rewrite.title: AI spend is a $53.7M lens inside the $650M budget, not an additive budget.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.executive_summary: The source-backed AI-tagged spend lens is $53.7M. It spans embedded platform AI, approved AI pilots, AI enablement foundations, governance controls, cloud AI services, and training/change activity.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.business_meaning: Tower can show where AI-related spend sits, but it must not add that lens on top of the technology budget.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.what_context_reveals: Platform spend such as Copilot, ServiceNow AI, Databricks, cloud AI services, and AI governance can support multiple use cases.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.why_it_matters: The lens helps a CIO manage AI investment without double-counting platform spend as a candidate use case budget.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.evidence_boundary: AI-tagged spend does not fund Member Service AI Assist or any other candidate unless an explicit source tie exists.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.recommended_next_action: Show AI spend by category with duplicate-counting caveats and separate candidate opportunities.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.measurement_posture: Usage and KPI measurement are required before value is claimable.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.value_claim_boundary: Embedded platform spend is not realized value.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.cio_implication: Treat AI spend as a portfolio management lens across platforms and use cases.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.cfo_implication: Keep the AI lens non-additive and reconcile it to budget and finance source rows.

story_blocks_to_rewrite.title: Approved programs must trace to budget and finance rows before Tower treats them as funded.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.executive_summary: The program portfolio view contains 12 approved source-adapter program rows with funding ties. Tower should show these as funded programs only when budget or finance source links resolve.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.business_meaning: This prevents a program list from becoming a budget claim without reconciliation.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.what_context_reveals: Program portfolio rows carry linked budget and finance references that can be traced into the budget and spend layer.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.why_it_matters: Program funding is the bridge between executive intent and financial control.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.evidence_boundary: Approved program funding is source-backed where links exist; it is not the same as delivered value.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.recommended_next_action: Audit any approved/active program without a budget or finance tie before showing it in Tower.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.financial_posture: Program funding is shown only when tied to budget or finance source rows.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.measurement_posture: Program delivery and benefits need separate KPI and benefits-ledger evidence.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.value_claim_boundary: Funded program does not equal realized value.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.cio_implication: Use the program map to focus execution governance.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.cfo_implication: Use the finance ties to enforce budget accountability.

story_blocks_to_rewrite.title: Candidate AI opportunities are readiness items until funded and measured.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.executive_summary: Tower can show 242 candidate/discovery AI opportunities as a readiness portfolio. It must not present one use case as the selected solution or imply candidate funding.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.business_meaning: The CIO sees the opportunity landscape; Moves later selects and shapes one or more business cases.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.what_context_reveals: Some platform AI pilots are approved, while candidate business opportunities remain opportunity-only.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.why_it_matters: This keeps AI portfolio governance honest and prevents accidental business-case approval.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.evidence_boundary: Candidate opportunities are not funded programs without explicit source linkage.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.recommended_next_action: Prioritize candidates by baseline readiness, control readiness, data-domain availability, and business owner commitment.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.financial_posture: Candidate rows carry zero approved funding unless source rows state otherwise.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.measurement_posture: Most candidate rows require baseline and KPI evidence.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.value_claim_boundary: No candidate value may be shown as realized.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.cio_implication: Use the matrix to choose where to run discovery and where to wait for data/control maturity.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.cfo_implication: Keep platform AI spend separate from candidate use-case value claims.

story_blocks_to_rewrite.title: Measurement readiness is the gate between value hypothesis and value claim.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.executive_summary: Tower can show budget, program, candidate, and benefits posture, but it should require usage, KPI, and finance validation before a value claim becomes claimable.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.business_meaning: The dashboard should tell executives what must be measured next, not inflate benefits.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.what_context_reveals: The benefits ledger contains promised value, usage actuals where available, KPI actuals where available, finance validation amounts, and value claim status.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.why_it_matters: CIO/CFO trust depends on seeing the boundary between promise and evidence.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.evidence_boundary: Partial usage or KPI evidence alone is not full finance validation.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.recommended_next_action: Prioritize benefits with missing usage, KPI, or finance validation evidence.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.financial_posture: $3.8M finance-validated value is loaded; promised value remains separate.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.measurement_posture: Usage/KPI/finance validation status is derived from benefits-ledger raw fields.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.value_claim_boundary: Promised value is not realized value.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.cio_implication: Use measurement readiness to decide which initiatives need operating discipline before scale.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.cfo_implication: Require finance validation before board reporting.

story_blocks_to_rewrite.title: The benefits ledger separates promised value from finance-validated value.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.executive_summary: The benefits ledger carries $35.5M promised value posture and $3.8M finance-validated value. Promised value is not realized value.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.business_meaning: Tower should show benefit readiness and claim gates, not inflated ROI.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.what_context_reveals: Usage, KPI, and finance validation vary by program; claimable status is explicit.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.why_it_matters: CIO/CFO trust depends on separating promise, usage, KPI movement, and finance validation.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.evidence_boundary: Do not roll promised benefit values into Tower hero KPIs.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.recommended_next_action: Ask finance and operational owners to validate usage/KPI extracts before claiming value.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.financial_posture: $3.8M finance validated out of $35.5M promised posture.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.measurement_posture: Partial measured posture exists for some pilots; others are baseline/readiness only.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.value_claim_boundary: Promised benefit value is not realized value.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.cio_implication: Use the benefits ledger to manage the benefit operating cadence.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.cfo_implication: Require finance validation before any savings or ROI language.

story_blocks_to_rewrite.title: The CIO/CFO conversation should be about budget control, evidence gates, and measured adoption.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.executive_summary: The strongest executive story is not a savings claim. It is a governed operating cadence: keep the $650M budget reconciled, manage the $53.7M AI lens without double counting, separate approved programs from candidate opportunities, and make value claims only after benefits validation.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.business_meaning: Tower becomes a value-realization control room rather than a dashboard of aspirational numbers.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.what_context_reveals: The source packet has enough structure to show where spend, programs, AI candidates, and benefit claims connect.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.why_it_matters: That gives the CIO and CFO a common fact base for funding, measurement, and governance.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.evidence_boundary: This is an executive interpretation of source-backed context, not a new fact.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.recommended_next_action: Run the next review around three gates: budget reconciliation, candidate AI readiness, and benefit validation.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.financial_posture: Budget is source-backed; value is validation-gated.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.measurement_posture: Adoption, KPI, and finance validation are the next operating discipline.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.value_claim_boundary: No ROI, savings, or realized value without evidence.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.cio_implication: Use Tower to decide what to protect, what to measure, and what not to overclaim.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.cfo_implication: Use Tower to enforce evidence-backed value claims before executive reporting.

story_blocks_to_rewrite.title: Tower should convert raw gaps into executive blockers.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.executive_summary: The main Tower blockers are baseline validation, actuals, finance validation, source-system lineage, workflow evidence, PHI/control posture, program-budget tie gaps, and AI duplicate-counting risk.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.business_meaning: Executives need a short blocker list, not hundreds of row-level caveats.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.what_context_reveals: Most value claims are blocked by measurement evidence, not by lack of narrative.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.why_it_matters: This keeps the dashboard from looking polished while the evidence base remains incomplete.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.evidence_boundary: Gaps are source-derived and must remain visible.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.recommended_next_action: Assign blockers to finance, operations, data, security, and program owners before using Tower as a board artifact.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.financial_posture: No gap closure, no value claim.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.measurement_posture: Baseline and actual evidence are required before measured-outcome language.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.value_claim_boundary: Blocked claims stay blocked until the required evidence resolves.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.cio_implication: Use blockers to organize remediation work.
story_blocks_to_rewrite.cfo_implication: Use blockers to control external value reporting.
